solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: You're apprehended — the consequence of a beating?

definitions.meaning: an idiom said when a wrongdoer is caught and the pretence is over
on a shoot, beaters drive the birds and animals hunted for sport up into the air, so after a beating the quarry rises

explanation.surface: A policeman collaring someone and noting that being caught follows a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beating' suggests violence, but it is the shooting-party sense: beaters flush birds into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a caught culprit is told their deception has been exposed, and flushed game birds literally rise.

clue.text: Bible translator foremost in Tewkesbury and Ely, possibly

indicators.note: the front letter of the town name Tewkesbury is taken
possibly signals the letters of and Ely may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A translator associated with two English cathedral towns, Tewkesbury and Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ANDELY into YNDALE after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tyndale made the first printed English translation of the New Testament in the 1520s.

clue.text: Become very angry, being clean upset over end of it

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: clean means pure

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word it

explanation.surface: Someone flying into a rage because a cleaning job has been spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PURE into ERUP; 'over' simply places it above T in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up suddenly in temper, as a volcano bursts out, is a figurative synonym.

clue.text: A Queen looking down on opponent's appearance

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit above what follows

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
an opponent is a rival

explanation.surface: A queen gazing disdainfully at how her rival looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' tempts as looks, but it means coming on the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: making an appearance is turning up, the act of getting somewhere.

clue.text: Each girl getting cut exhibits pain

parts.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price tags

indicators.note: getting cut means the name loses its tail letter

parts.note: Rachel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Every girl who is wounded shows that she is hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache inside the ear is a particular kind of physical hurt.

clue.text: Military position: to fight after second incursion

indicators.note: after places the word for fighting behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: an incursion is an entry into territory
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A battle plan: go to war once a second invasion has happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard's hut where a soldier stands watch is a post on military duty.

clue.text: Room's dangerous, missing end, right?

indicators.note: missing end means the word drops its final letter

parts.note: parlous means perilous or dangerous

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a room is unsafe because it lacks a finishing touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Room stands for 'is', a link; 'dangerous' tempts as a description of the room but supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room for receiving guests in a house is the traditional sense.

clue.text: Deployment of line or a gun shows weakness

indicators.note: deployment arranges troops, so these letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Positioning one row of troops or one artillery piece shows a lack of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deployment of' rearranges L, OR, A and GUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude, a tired lack of vigour, is close to feebleness of body or spirit.

clue.text: Long sentence always found in part of book indicating national honour

parts.note: life imprisonment is the longest prison sentence

indicators.note: found in puts the poetic word for always inside the book part

parts.note: a page is part of a book
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A book passage about a long jail term pointing to a national distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-hereditary seat in the House of Lords is a state honour conferred in Britain.

clue.text: Scripture lessons given by Father in modern Scots town

parts.note: RE is religious education, school scripture lessons

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for Father inside the word for modern

parts.note: new means modern
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest teaches religion in an up-to-date Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Renfrew is a town near Glasgow on the Clyde, in western Scotland.

clue.text: Dentist's targets: modest, white, drilled

indicators.note: drilled means put through drills and reorganised, signalling these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dentist's aim: neat, white teeth that have been drilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drilled' looks like dentistry, but it rearranges MODEST and WHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Third molars often need extracting, so they are frequent objects of a dentist's work.

clue.text: Description of sprinter consuming energy meal

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the energy letter goes inside

parts.note: a sprinter is described as fast
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A runner eating something for energy before a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is a large, lavish spread of food, an elaborate repast.

clue.text: Spiteful, throttling one King instead of another

indicators.note: throttling means gripping round the neck, so the word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: vicious means spiteful or malicious
a means one
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A malicious person strangles one monarch to replace him with another.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced through someone else, on their behalf rather than in person: a substitute sense.

clue.text: Prince and Queen featuring in part of movie (earlier instalment)

indicators.note: featuring in puts the queen's abbreviation inside the film part

parts.note: a reel is a section of film

explanation.surface: Royal characters appear in a section of a film, which is itself a backstory episode.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or story set before an existing one, made afterwards, is an earlier part in sequence.

clue.text: In trouble? That's the standard position!

definitions.meaning: a British slang phrase for in difficulty or gone wrong
a standard is a flag, which is hoisted to the top of its staff

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is in a fix, then answering with the usual stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like normal, but it means a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for in a mess, and literally where a flag sits when flown.

clue.text: Ban doctor probing part of head and leave

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so the doctor goes inside

parts.note: the ear is part of the head
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
go means leave

explanation.surface: A doctor examining an ear is barred and told to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition, especially on trade with a country, is a formal prohibition order.

clue.text: Flexible shop transaction, backed to take less than a second

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sale is a transaction in a shop

indicators.note: less than means short of its last letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A shop deal that is reversed in under a second is adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SALE into ELAS; 'less than' trims TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy and springing back, a pliable material bends easily: a synonym.

clue.text: Pistol, say — nice shot — carried by soldier

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the soldier

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker ant, and ant is a common crossword soldier

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, signalling these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pistol, a nice shot, borne by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pistol' is not a gun but Shakespeare's Ancient Pistol, an ensign; 'shot' rearranges NICE to NCIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare an ensign is called an ancient, and Pistol holds that rank in Henry V.

clue.text: A fast runner, he gets ahead of Greek character entering church

indicators.note: entering puts the pieces inside the church
gets ahead of puts the pronoun before the Greek letter

parts.note: taken as written
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A quick racer overtakes a Greek inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The big spotted cat is the speediest land animal, a sprinter of the savannah.

clue.text: Old navigational tool, special and still in use

parts.note: extant means still existing

explanation.surface: An antique instrument that is unusual and still being used.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument measuring the angle of the sun above the horizon was used to find latitude at sea.

clue.text: Shifty lawyer, mostly unrelenting after trial

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word behind the attempt

parts.note: a shy is a try or attempt, as at a coconut shy

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: stern means unrelenting

explanation.surface: A dodgy lawyer, mostly ruthless, once the court case is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' tempts as a court case; it means an attempt. 'mostly' trims STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an unscrupulous practitioner, especially of law: a dishonest attorney.

clue.text: Source of protein — meal dished up with bun

indicators.note: dished up suggests food served in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protein-rich meal served alongside a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg white is largely protein, so it is a dietary supply of it.

clue.text: Many cheer Rocky's opponent

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Crowds applaud the boxer Rocky's rival in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like the film boxer, but it rearranges MANY CHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief foe is the principal adversary, the main rival one faces.

clue.text: Film star contributing to many a good house?

definitions.meaning: Clark ... was a Hollywood leading man of Gone with the Wind

definitions.text: contributing to many a good house
definitions.meaning: the triangular end wall under a pitched roof is part of many houses

explanation.surface: A movie star helping to build plenty of fine homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a screen idol, and a pitched roof ends in a triangular wall.

clue.text: Author audiobook confuses with Sterne?

indicators.note: an audiobook is heard rather than read, so similar-sounding names get mixed up

parts.note: the novelist's name Sterne is said like stern, and stern means grim

explanation.surface: Listening to a recording, one author is mistaken for Laurence Sterne.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterne is heard as stern, a synonym of grim, which in turn is heard as the author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brothers Grimm, Jacob and Wilhelm, compiled and wrote the famous German fairy tales.

clue.text: Take up level position, being still unconscious

parts.note: even means still or level, as in even water
out means knocked unconscious

explanation.surface: Someone lying flat while out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To become flat or steady, as prices or a graph do, is to settle level.

clue.text: Old car journey hard? Little hesitation getting on board

indicators.note: getting on board means boarding, going inside the other pieces

parts.note: a trip is a journey
um is a brief sound of hesitation
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A drive in a vintage car is a struggle, with a moment's pause before boarding.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumph was a British car maker whose marque, now defunct, built the TR sports cars.

clue.text: Film bloke in field chasing most of them

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the fielder comes after
most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
third man is a cricket fielding position, a man in the field

explanation.surface: A movie about a man in a field pursuing a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position behind the batter on the off side; 'most of' cuts THEM to THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol Reed's 1949 thriller set in Vienna, starring Orson Welles as Harry Lime.
